subject: Latency spike: cross-region routing misfire causing p95/p99 surge
messages:
From: Nina Park <nina.park@horizonpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@horizonpay.com
Date: 2026-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe latency spike affecting payments endpoints (p95/p99)

Soojin —

We started seeing a major latency regression on the Redwood Hosted API for our production route (region: us-west-2) starting ~2026-07-28 08:45 UTC. p95 has jumped from ~120ms to 520ms and p99 is hitting multiple seconds. Error rate is slightly elevated (2–3%), throughput (req/s) stayed about the same.

Attached: horizonpay_p95_graph_20260728.png (png) showing timeline and sample traces. We rely on low tail latency for real-time authorizations; this is causing transaction timeouts in our flow. Can you confirm what changed on your side?

Please escalate; this is affecting customers.

—Nina
VP Engineering, HorizonPay

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Nina Park <nina.park@horizonpay.com>
Date: 2026-07-28T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency spike affecting payments endpoints (p95/p99)

Thanks for flagging, Nina — I’m on it and have looped in Marcus (infra on-call) and Jonas (SRE lead).

Marcus/Jonas: please triage routing + gateway configs immediately. Customer sees p95/p99 spikes starting ~08:45 UTC; traffic volume unchanged. Evelyn, FYI (CS).

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: confirm if any routing policy or config pushed around 08:30–09:00 UTC (UTC times in logs) that could cause cross-region routing or rebalancing.
- Jonas: check runtime stack/middleware for changes that could increase RTT (e.g., gateway standby pool, TLS handshakes, proxy behaviour).

I’ll coordinate comms with Nina while we investigate.

—Soojin
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency spike affecting payments endpoints (p95/p99) — initial triage

Quick update from infra: we found a routing policy change that was deployed at 08:39 UTC by an automated rollout.

Symptoms and evidence:
- HAProxy routing table shows a recent modification to the smart-routing policy key for HorizonPay's account that loosened region affinity.
- A/B policy change pushed a fallback route to eu-central-1 for a subset of ephemeral tokens (approx 18% of connections), which explains the RTT jump and higher tail latency.
- No application-level change or model rollout in that window.

Snippet from haproxy-routing-snippet.txt (attached) shows the policy line: "route_pref: dynamic,region_affinity: soft" — this was intended for a non-critical internal test but the rollout scope accidentally included production HorizonPay routes.

Immediate action taken:
- Disabled the automated rollout targeting flag at 10:01 UTC to stop further propagation.
- Rebalanced connections to respect region affinity while we validate draining.

Next steps: revert the policy on the customer’s route and trigger connection drain to restore US-origin serving. I estimate p95 should recover within 15–25 minutes after drains complete.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer (on-call)
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Nina Park <nina.park@horizonpay.com>
Date: 2026-07-28T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency spike affecting payments endpoints (p95/p99) — mitigation plan

Thanks Marcus — good catch. Recommended mitigation:
1) Immediate rollback of the smart-routing change for HorizonPay (done if Marcus confirms).
2) Force regional-affinity on active sessions for 30 minutes (manual override) to avoid repeated cross-region failover.
3) Increase prefix cache TTL and enable sticky-session hints for the customer’s API key to reduce reconnections during drain.
4) Run a controlled canary to confirm p95/p99 drop before full close.

I’ll coordinate a short maintenance window and monitor tails. If p95/p99 does not recover within 40 minutes, escalate to execs for temporary credits and further compensatory actions.

—Jonas
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Park <nina.park@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Severe latency spike affecting payments endpoints (p95/p99) — status update

Nina —

Thanks for your patience. Quick summary: our infra team identified an unintended routing policy rollout that loosened region affinity, causing ~18% of your traffic to route to eu-central-1 (higher RTT). Marcus has disabled the rollout and we’re reverting the policy for HorizonPay now. We expect visible p95 improvement within ~20 minutes as connections drain and re-establish to us-west-2.

Immediate offers from Redwood: 
- We will provide a credit for the affected window and work with you on a postmortem with timeline + remediation.
- If you prefer, we can enact a short region-affinity maintenance window and push a post-deployment validation gate for your account to prevent this class of issue.

Can you confirm whether you observed any downstream customer-facing transaction failures beyond what you shared? Also please confirm the time window you want considered for credits (we will propose 08:45–11:00 UTC by default).

—Soojin
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, VP_Operations <vp.operations@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec brief: HorizonPay latency incident — request for review and approval of credits

Team —

Summary (for execs):
- Incident: p95/p99 latency spike for HorizonPay observed 2026-07-28 08:45 UTC — caused by a mis-scoped routing policy rollout that relaxed region affinity and routed ~18% of production connections to eu-central-1.
- Impact: elevated p95 from ~120ms -> ~520ms; p99 multi-second; error rate up to 3%; customer transaction timeouts reported.
- Root cause: automated smart-routing rollout (intended for internal testing) included production scope due to a tagging bug.
- Mitigation: rollout disabled and policy reverted; connections drained and rebalanced to us-west-2; prefix-cache TTL adjustments applied. p95 returned to baseline within ~30 minutes after rollback.
- Customer touch: We offered credits for window 08:45–11:00 UTC; customer awaiting confirmation.

Request: approval for a $35k credit (per existing SLO compensation matrix) and sign-off to run a joint postmortem with HorizonPay. Also recommend we add an explicit production-exclusion flag to automatic rollouts and a pre-rollout scope verification step.

I will attach a draft postmortem and owner assignments (mitigation doc: mitigation_plan.docx).

—Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
